items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Don Redmond first was the director and arranger... he said, 'I would like to use you in the band as pianist, and arranger...'

ctx.x: This is April 12, 1975 in Denver, Colorado, interview with Horace Henderson. Horace, we're just checking out some of the information that we've gained from other books, and one book that I have indicates that -- let's see, in the year 1931, Don Redmond, who apparently had been playing in your band, became the leader for a period of time, and that you continued with him for about another year and a half, up until 19 -- early 1933. Is that correct?

No, that isn't quite correct. I'll tell you. Don Redmond first was the director and arranger for the great McKinney's Cottonpickers Band in Detroit, Michigan, the Graystone Ballroom. And Don has been -- (inaudible) I should say, because it's past tense now -- was always aggressive in getting a good job. Don got a contract in New York City in a nightclub called Connie's Inn. He got the contract first, and began to search for the band, McKinney's so he gave his notice with the Cottonpickers as director. So

he found out that I was playing in a place in Columbus, Ohio called Valley Dale. I had an excellent band there, and he came over and came out and heard the band, and loved it. Then we talked about what he had in mind, and he said, "I have a contract in New York City at Connie's Inn, and he said, 'It's gonna be a long time contract. The Mills Brothers will be a feature there, and he said, 'You'll have to relinquish your ownership of the band, and naturally your name, but I would like to use you in the band as…
